record.original_question: If two spherical space forms have the same length spectrum of closed geodesics, must they be quotient commensurable, meaning that both arise as finite-index quotients inside a common finite group generated by their deck groups?

evidence.quote: Question 8.9. If two spherical space forms have the same length spectrum, must they be quotient commensurable?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A spherical space form is a closed Riemannian manifold of constant sectional curvature +1, equivalently a quotient S^n/Γ, where S^n is the round n-sphere and Γ is a finite subgroup of O(n+1) acting freely on S^n. The length spectrum of such a manifold is the multiset of lengths of its closed geodesics, counted with multiplicities.

Say that two spherical space forms M_1 = S^n/Γ_1 and M_2 = S^n/Γ_2 are quotient commensurable if there exists a finite subgroup G of O(n+1) acting freely on S^n such that both Γ_1 and Γ_2 are subgroups of G (so that M_1 and M_2 are both finite-index quotients of the common spherical space form S^n/⟨e⟩ covering S^n/G, in the sense that they share a common finite-sheeted Riemannian cover/quotient structure inside G).

Question: If two spherical space forms have the same length spectrum of closed geodesics, must they be quotient commensurable?

artifact.status_search_result: The question appears as an explicitly posed open question in recent work on isospectral spherical space forms. Related recent papers (2024–2026) continue to study isospectral and length-isospectral spherical space forms and their commensurability properties, but no resolution of the quotient-commensurability question for length-isospectral spherical space forms is reported in the search results.

status_evidence.snippet: Recent (2024) work studying isospectral spherical space forms.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent work studies isospectral spherical space forms without resolving the quotient-commensurability question.

status_evidence.title: The fundamental group of a spherical space form is not audible
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work showing the fundamental group is not determined by the spectrum.
status_evidence.claim: Related recent results indicate the spectrum does not determine fine algebraic structure, but the quotient commensurability question for the length spectrum is not settled here.
